title: Tabs
description: Every tab system, and one to unify them.

add.title: 1. ext/tabs — the shared engine
add.text:
**Path:** `framework/ext/tabs/tabs.js` + `tabs.css`.

**Extends / imports:** adds `Page.prototype.tabs` (imports `core/View` and `core/Page/Page.class.js`). Not a class.

**Used by:** `ext/Doc`, `core/Page/Frame.js` (`navigation: "tabs"`), `Columns.js`, `ext/tabs/switcher.js`, the generator, and about 100 demo pages.

**Style:** underlined flush tabs by default; `.block` = folder tabs; `.bounded` = boxed; `.vertical` = side rail; `.stick` = sticks on scroll. Title-inline does NOT come from here: the host adds it (Doc and the AI head do).

The bar is always one row that scrolls sideways.

add.title: ext/tabs use
2. ext/Doc — top tabs beside the title
add.text:
**Path:** `framework/ext/Doc/Doc.js` (+ `Doc.css`, `ClassDoc.js`).

**Extends:** yes, `class Doc extends Page`; `ClassDoc extends Doc`. Imports `../tabs/tabs.js`, `PageWork`, `PageInbox`, `catalog`.

**Used by:** every module's Docs page (about 39 pages, e.g. `core/Page`, `ext/tabs`), via `ClassDoc` for class pages.

**Style:** `ext/tabs` `.tabs.block.stick` with `Doc.css`: `.doc-well` holds the h1, and `.page.doc-page > .tabs { display: contents }` puts the strip on the same flex line. **Title-inline works here.** Nested Docs get `.vertical` rails.

add.title: Doc.render()
3. /framework/ai/ head — hand-built copy
add.text:
**Path:** `framework/ai/page.js`, `head()`.

**Extends / imports:** a POJO page, not a class. Builds `div.c("tabs block stick")` and `tab-bar` by hand; imports `AIOverview` (`detectTabs`), not `tabs()`.

**Used by:** every page under `/framework/ai/` (dashboard, Inbox, Tasks).

**Style:** same `ext/tabs` classes. CSS: `ux/Inbox/Inbox.css` (`.inbox-head`, copies `.doc-well`) and `ai/rail/rail.css`. **Title-inline works**; a second implementation of Doc's look.

add.title: AI head()
4. LivePage.Tabs — the /live/ row
add.text:
**Path:** `public/live/LivePage.js` (`static Tabs = class LiveTabsView extends View`, `tabs_of()`), CSS `public/live/LivePage.css`.

**Extends / imports:** `LivePage extends Page`; Tabs extends `View`. Does not import `tabs()`: reuses only the `.tabs`, `.tab-bar`, `.tab` classes and `ext/tabs` CSS.

**Used by:** `/live/` and its sub-pages marked `{"tab":true}` (max 5, else link cards).

**Style:** smaller `.live-tabs` with edge fades. The h1 and tab row are two stacked rows (`.live-head-row`, then the tabs). **Title-inline does not apply here yet**; it would need a `.live-head` flex line.

add.title: LivePage tabs
5. Page navigation: "tabs" and tab lines
add.text:
**Path:** `framework/core/Page/Frame.js` (calls `page.tabs`), `Columns.js`, `Log.js`/`Jsonl.js` (`tab` lines: `nav`, `disabled`, `order`, `title`).

**Extends / imports:** methods on `Page`; they fall back to a muted note if `ext/tabs` was never imported (core never imports ext).

**Used by:** any page whose `page.jsonl` says `navigation: tabs`; `/live/demos/tabs-page/`.

**Style:** plain `ext/tabs` flush look. No title-inline: a page shown as a tab hides its own h1.

add.title: page.jsonl, as JS
6. Hand-rolled copies of the same markup
add.text:
**Paths:** `framework/ai/AITask/AITask.js` (`tab_bar()`, buttons that toggle panels), `framework/ai/cards/card.js` (card tab strip), `framework/ai/tasks/TaskLanes.js` (`TaskLanes.tabs`).

**Extends / imports:** none of them call `tabs()`; they write `div.c("tabs")`, `tab-bar`, `tab` themselves. `card.js` imports `ext/tabs/tabs.js` only for its stylesheet.

**Used by:** task pages, AI cards, the Tasks lanes page.

**Style:** `ext/tabs` CSS. Not routed: state is in memory, so `?tab` links and reload do not return you to a tab.

add.title: AITask tab_bar()
7. DrawerTabs — the ☰ sheet
add.text:
**Path:** `framework/ext/drawer/tabs.js` (`class DrawerTabs`; tabs in `drawer/tabs/*.js`, CSS in `drawer.css`).

**Extends / imports:** extends nothing; imports `drawer.js`, `ext/Ask`, `View`. Each tab lazy-loads its own file.

**Used by:** `drawer/Sheet.js`, the ☰ menu on every page.

**Style:** its own small row of tabs in the drawer, routed as `?drawer=<name>`. Not `ext/tabs` and not title-inline.

add.title: DrawerTabs list
8. SwipeTabs — phone panes
add.text:
**Path:** `framework/ai/sessions/v/mobile/SwipeTabs.js` + `mobile.css`.

**Extends / imports:** `extends View`; imports `View`.

**Used by:** `MobileSession.js` (Overview, Tasks, Chat), `/framework/ai/sessions/v/mobile/`.

**Style:** `.mob-tabs`: a button row over a scroll-snap strip; swiping lights the tab. Not routed, not `ext/tabs`.

add.title: SwipeTabs
9. page.ui.tabs — a saved tab bar item
add.text:
**Path:** `public/live/design/ui/Tabs.js` (`Tabs extends Item`, `Tabs.View extends View`), registered in `PageUI`.

**Extends / imports:** `Item`, `View`, `PageUI`.

**Used by:** the `/live/design/` lab only.

**Style:** `.page-ui-tabs` buttons in `DesignPage.css`. It stores `selected` in the page log, so a reload keeps the tab. Its own look, not `ext/tabs`.

add.title: page.ui.tabs delta
10. switcher — vertical tabs wrapper
add.text:
**Path:** `framework/ext/tabs/switcher.js`.

**Extends / imports:** adds `Page.prototype.switcher`; imports `tabs.js`. It is just `this.tabs(names).ac("vertical")`.

**Used by:** `core/Page/layout/switcher/` demos. **Style:** left rail, flips to a row under 64em.

add.title: Unify?
add.text:
Six of the ten systems already draw the same `.tabs` / `.tab-bar` / `.tab` markup. Only the code that builds it and the title-inline CSS are copied.

**A. Make `ext/tabs` own title-inline.** Add a `tabs({ title })` option (or a `.tabs.inline` class) that moves Doc's `.doc-well` + `display: contents` CSS into `tabs.css`. Doc, the AI head and `LivePage.Tabs` call it. Cheapest; fixes the duplicated CSS and gives /live/ the inline look. Tradeoff: still two builders (routed `tabs()` and hand-rolled).

**B. One `Tabs` class** (`ext/tabs/Tabs.js`, extends `View`): takes `[{label, href|panel}]`, with routed and in-memory modes. `Page.prototype.tabs` becomes a thin caller; AITask, card.js, TaskLanes, LivePage and the AI head use it. Cleanest; matches "one of everything". Tradeoff: most work, about 100 call sites to keep working, and the live-update redraw hooks must move across.

**C. Leave the odd ones separate** (DrawerTabs, SwipeTabs, page.ui.tabs) and do only A plus the hand-rolled copies in B. Tradeoff: they stay different looks, but they need swipe, lazy-load and saved state that the routed engine does not.

My lean: A first, then B for the hand-rolled five.
